unit.title: Проект: приложение для рисования с Tkinter

learning_outcomes.statement: The learner can build a real Tkinter Canvas application: distinguish the app's document model from Canvas's own retained items, implement multiple drawing tools with correct coordinate geometry, maintain an undo/redo history, and safely persist/restore the document as JSON

reviewers.display_name: Claude Sonnet 5 — M01-I04 Batch E assistant analyst
reviewers.attestation: Read the chapter's canonical builder in full (all lesson-builder functions), coordinated specialist sub-reviews that cross-checked every printed/claimed code result by executing the corresponding snippets under the project's own Python 3.14.6 venv (xvfb for tkinter/turtle/pygame), ran every canonical notebook via scripts/run_notebook.py, independently re-verified every grader's expected value against both a correct and an incorrect solution, applied every confirmed BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR remediation, and confirmed the canonical source and review-surface sha256 values match the current committed state exactly.

criteria.rationale: All 32 theory lessons were read in full and every executable/numeric claim was independently re-executed under Python 3.14.6; every confirmed defect (including no chapter-opener-level blocker; the most severe defect (unsafe error handling in the project's own load path) was chapter-scoped and is now fixed) was fixed and re-verified.
Python-3.14/library-version-specific behaviours (Tk/Tcl, turtle, pygame-ce as applicable) verified against the actual installed interpreter and toolkit under xvfb.
Chapter-specific terminology used precisely and consistently, matching real Russian-language usage for this subject area; extends the existing register additively.

The opener promises the Canvas mental model (retained items, not painted pixels), the Canvas coordinate system vs Turtle's, item ids and tags, mouse-gesture state, per-tool geometry, layering, undo/redo history, and JSON save/load of the drawing document; full-chapter reading confirms every promised topic is delivered (build a real Tkinter Canvas application: distinguish the app's document model from Canvas's own retained items, implement multiple drawing tools with correct coordinate geometry, maintain an undo/redo history, and safely persist/restore the document as JSON).
Claims are traceable to source and, where behavioural, to an actual re-execution recorded in this batch's evidence.

The opener states the chapter's scope (the Canvas mental model (retained items, not painted pixels), the Canvas coordinate system vs Turtle's, item ids and tags, mouse-gesture state, per-tool geometry, layering, undo/redo history, and JSON save/load of the drawing document) as concrete, checkable topics culminating in the paint-app project.

Assumes Chapter 17's Tkinter event/widget foundation, Chapter 15's JSON/file handling, and Chapters 6-7's Turtle coordinate system (contrasted explicitly, not silently reused). All genuinely available.
18.8's mental-model section is the chapter's strongest conceptual anchor: it explains up front why everything later (undo, editing, layering) is even possible, before any of those features appear.

32 sections chunk into a first working prototype (18.1-18.7), then 'Canvas properly' (mental model, coordinates, ids/tags, gestures), then tools/appearance, then history/persistence, then the final project -- not one undifferentiated list.
18.32's Paint Pro closes the arc with a four-column readiness checklist (model/tools/history/persistence) verified against the shipped code, matching the structure the chapter actually taught.
Terminology and patterns established in earlier chapters are explicitly and correctly reused, not re-derived or re-explained inconsistently.
Internal cross-references (forward and backward) were checked and verified accurate once the referenced sections were themselves reviewed; incorrect ones found in this batch were fixed.

Fixed a real defect where load_from_path() destroyed the current document and its undo history before the malformed-JSON error was even raised, leaving the app permanently wedged -- corrected to check for errors before mutating state, matching the pattern Chapter 15 already establishes for JSONDecodeError.
Chapter number, title, and all section identifiers match the PAGES navigation model and sidebar exactly.
